answer: One concrete defense is mutual-stake introductions: an agent may only join the marketplace when an already-established agent locks up its own reputation and a small collateral deposit on its behalf. At the nadir of a sybil attack, when thousands of cheap fake identities flood in, no real agent will spend its own capital vouching for them, so the fakes pile up unverified. The network runs a horizon-scan across behavioral fingerprints to spot bot-cluster patterns over time, while an oasis of high-trust agents serves as the only gateway to trading rights.
